TAGSOPS · META
15:02AI26 · GROK TUI · GROK BOT — Jared asked to add to the system prompt so every conversation — everything we talk about, everything he learns, everything he is curious about — is logged to jkw/AI26/. He wanted me to pick the file type and directory structure. He wants this session and all future terminal sessions to write there as verbosely as possible, so he can later reflect on his AI usage. He also wants a Grok Bot reading the same vault to produce daily, weekly, and quarterly summaries of why he spends so much time with AI and what the outcome is. He was in a Grok Build TUI session at /Users/jkw (home workspace). No existing ~/AI26, no ~/.grok/rules, no ~/.grok/hooks. He already had Grok Bot local-exec and LaunchAgents for other jobs (lid-awake, careerops).
OUTCOMEShipped the vault at /Users/jkw/AI26/ (markdown journal + jsonl events + learnings.md + curiosity.md + summaries/). Installed global Grok rule ~/.grok/rules/ai26-journal.md (symlink to AGENT.md) and hooks ~/.grok/hooks/ai26-journal.json. Installed Claude Code rule + CLAUDE.md pointer + settings.json hooks. Installed launchd jobs com.jkw.ai26-daily (21:00 ET), weekly (Sunday 21:30), quarterly (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct 1 10:00) running grok headless summarizer. Self-tested hook/note/redaction; grok inspect sees the rule and all 10 hook events. THIS current Grok session started before the rule/hooks existed, so automatic capture for remaining turns in this session is not guaranteed until he starts a new session.
LEARNEDGrok global system-prompt injection for all projects is ~/.grok/rules/*.md (always scanned), not only ~/.grok/AGENTS.md. Lifecycle hooks in ~/.grok/hooks/*.json fire on SessionStart/End, UserPromptSubmit, Stop (with lastAssistantMessage up to 32KiB), and tool events; Stop hooks must exit 0 or they block the agent. Claude Code user instructions live at ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md plus ~/.claude/rules/ and hooks can be merged into ~/.claude/settings.json. launchd StartCalendarInterval with Weekday=0 is Sunday; quarterly jobs take an array of month/day dicts. Secret-like strings in prompts can be regex-redacted before hitting the vault.

LEARNEDFDE job: technical product discovery through hands-on engineering (prototype in hours, sit with partner engineers, leave cookbook/eval/demo, file a platform ticket). Not consulting, not SA, not TAM. Two products never mix: Nebius AI Cloud (GPU IaaS, k8s, Soperator) vs Token Factory (OpenAI-compatible API at https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1). Dedicated TF endpoints are on-demand from a shared pool, not reservations; stop releases GPUs. Fast vs Base is same weights, speculative decoding, latency not a different brain. Serverless rate limits are dynamic 15-min buckets. TF has no TTS. Slurm is the batch scheduler (sbatch in, GPUs out). Soperator is Slurm + a Kubernetes operator (OSS nebius/soperator), AI Cloud only; jail is shared root FS; health checks drain bad GPU/IB nodes. Kubeflow is rewrite-to-YAML, not a synonym. A training job is a gang. Collectives (NCCL all-reduce) need every rank; one dead GPU poisons a multi-day run. Drain = stop new work then replace. Checkpoints must be on shared disk. Gang scheduling: 64-GPU job will not start on 63 idle GPUs. Bandwidth: HBM > NVLink (inside box, TAS tier-0, TP lives here) > InfiniBand (between boxes) > Ethernet. NCCL is the software; NVLink/IB are the cables. SXM is the datacenter GPU socket with NVLink (gpu-h200-sxm), not a library; L40S is PCIe. LoRA: freeze the model, train a small adapter (W+BA). Token Factory post-training. Not a smaller model. QLoRA: same adapter, 4-bit frozen base so a 70B can fit a smaller GPU. Q is the base. DP: copy the model, split the data (Llama 8B on 8xH200, NCCL all-reduce grads). TP: slice every layer, wants NVLink (Llama 70B ~140GB BF16 will not fit one 80GB H100, TP=8 on one SXM node). PP: split depth across nodes (405B stages over IB, bubble is idle fill). World size = TP x PP x DP (e.g. 8x4x4=128). Inference twin: prefill/TTFT vs decode/tok/s; KV grows with batch x context; his H200 concurrency 4 vs 32 moved 381 tok/s 21s TTFT to 2128 tok/s 3.8s TTFT. Config before SKU. vLLM usual path; SGLang when the checkpoint has a vision tower. Standing preference this week: after he learns a concept, persist it into the gym same turn and push main so Vercel updates. Encoded in nebius-fde-prep/AGENTS.md and ~/.grok/rules/nebius-fde-gym.md. AI26 vault at /Users/jkw/AI26 is the 2026 usage journal; agents must run ai26-note.py each turn (he asked this turn to backfill the FDE gym work).

English bulldogs are obesity-prone, brachycephalic, reflux-prone; breed feeding charts often put a 40–50 lb adult at ~700–1,100 kcal depending on source and activity, split twice daily. 18:14AI26 — Jared, in the AI26 folder: 'we got a bunch of agents writing a bunch of stuff. are they just writing .md or is there something like machine code? machine markdown files or something way more efficient than just mark down? we pushin flat files or are we writing to a database?' He wants to know the actual storage model of the vault — human markdown vs machine format vs DB.
OUTCOMEAnswered from README.md, SCHEMA.md, ai26_lib.py, and live sizes. No code change.
LEARNEDAI26 is dual-write flat files, no database. Machine layer is daily JSONL at events/YYYY/MM/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl (one JSON object per line, append-only, flock). Human layer is journal/*.md plus learnings.md/curiosity.md/summaries. Third layer raw/ is byte-for-byte Claude/Grok transcripts (~1.2G of the 1.2G vault). Chrome/Safari/Brave history is *read from* those browsers' SQLite DBs then *written into* JSONL; the vault itself is not SQLite. Grok session_search.sqlite exists only inside the raw mirror. No parquet, no vector DB, no 'machine markdown'.
CURIOUSDoes he want to stay on JSONL forever, or later compact events into SQLite/DuckDB/parquet for query? Is the 1.2G raw/ mirror something he wants to prune vs keep as disaster recovery?
WHY AIInference: he wanted a walk of his own vault architecture while agents are dumping into it, rather than opening SCHEMA.md himself.
TAGSOPS · LEARNING

Venus is the eve + Next.js wedding-planner agent in ~/wedding (Vercel project vendor-scout, repo jaredwerba/vendor-scout). It had two gates: a shared ACCESS_CODE exchanged for an httpOnly vs_code cookie (app/unlock/page.tsx + app/api/unlock/route.ts, checked by every server page and by an accessCode() AuthFn in agent/channels/eve.ts), and a required email field on the landing (the opening message to Venus carried the email). I replaced accessCode() with publicLink() (every chat request accepted as the shared 'couple' principal; kept the KV daily request cap of 2000 as the only throttle), removed the cookie redirects from /, /my-wedding, /curated, /curated/[id], deleted /unlock and /api/unlock, added a next.config redirect /unlock -> /, stripped the email input and validation from VenusLanding (button is always shown, onBegin(budget) only), and rewrote agent/instructions.md so Venus asks for first names + a reply email inside the signature question, asks once more before outreach if still missing, never nags. README + agent.ts comments updated; ACCESS_CODE dropped from .env.local. Typecheck initially failed on stale .next/dev/types referencing the deleted routes; cleared them, typecheck + next build green. Committed as 'Venus v16: open to the world' (b4e2cd0) and pushed to main, which auto-deployed production. Discovered along the way that the project also has Vercel Deployment Protection 'Standard' (ssoProtection all_except_custom_domains): the generated vendor-scout-jared-werbas-projects.vercel.app URL bounces to Vercel login, but the real production domain vendor-scout-xi.vercel.app is public. The claude.ai Vercel MCP connector returned 403 for this project, so I used the CLI token against the REST API to read protection settings.
OUTCOMEShipped and verified live: commit b4e2cd0 deployed (READY) to vendor-scout-xi.vercel.app; / , /my-wedding, /curated return 200 with no cookie, /unlock 307s to /, eve chat routes answer 400/404 (not 401) without any cookie. Vercel-side SSO protection left as-is (previews protected, prod public) and flagged to Jared with an offer to disable. ACCESS_CODE env var left in Vercel, unused.
LEARNEDVercel 'Standard Protection' (ssoProtection.deploymentType=all_except_custom_domains) protects the generated *-<team>.vercel.app and git-branch aliases but NOT the project's own production domain (here vendor-scout-xi.vercel.app) — so a public link works while preview URLs still need Vercel login. Next 16 keeps generated route validators under .next/dev/types and .next/types; deleting a route leaves stale validators that break tsc until they are cleared or rebuilt. In eve, an AuthFn that returns a principal unconditionally is enough to open a channel; the cookie was the only thing gating chat requests.
CURIOUSShould Vercel Authentication be turned off entirely so any deployment link (not just vendor-scout-xi.vercel.app) is public? Should Venus stop asking for an email at all, or is 'ask once, never nag' the right call for a public demo? With OUTREACH_MODE=test in prod the public app only emails the test inbox — is Jared going to flip it to live now that strangers can drive it? The unused ACCESS_CODE env var is still set in all three Vercel environments.
WHY AIInferred: a cross-cutting removal touching auth, UI, agent instructions, docs, deploy verification, and a Vercel platform setting — faster to delegate end-to-end than to hand-trace every cookie check and re-verify production.

He approved the plan and I built it. Shipped as v18 (commit 93db25d) plus a fix commit (5ddce55). The big architectural move, straight from the Sentinel blueprint: research stopped being eve's built-in `agent` tool (a copy of the root that INHERITED send_outreach — a researcher one bad inference away from emailing a stranger) and became a declared subagent at agent/subagents/scout with a tool surface of exactly web_search + record_vendor. It cannot email anyone because the capability is absent, not forbidden. Second move: record_vendor writes each verified vendor to KV the moment it is found instead of returning one closing JSON blob, so a truncated run keeps what it found and 'recorded 0' becomes a detectable failure rather than an empty result indistinguishable from an empty market — Sentinel's record_finding pattern. Added get_research (joins findings to the live trace, reports per-specialist health so Venus re-runs a truncated category once and never invents a vendor to fill a gap), a durable per-session search budget (25 specialist / 40 root, cap_reached is a normal outcome), and real cost accounting. On observability: eve's parent stream deliberately carries only subagent.called and the final action.result — nothing a child does reaches the parent — so the browser now attaches directly to each specialist's own /eve/v1/session/:id/stream, the same trick eve's dev TUI uses. Built use-agent-lanes.ts (capped at 5 concurrent attachments, rehydrates from KV after reload) and observability-rail.tsx: the agent-stack diagram, a Plan/Act/Observe/Decide strip, one card per agent with live counters, and a dense event log with real inter-event latency from meta.at. Made it permanent on the right at lg+ (a bottom sheet below that) rather than behind the old 'under the hood' toggle, exactly as Jared asked. Rewrote the trace store to record the whole tree child->root and to REDACT at write time — no message text ever, since /observe is public by his earlier decision. LangSmith went live: set the key + LANGSMITH_TRACING=true in Vercel production (the exporter silently no-ops without the second), and wrote a transformExportedSpan that maps eve's ai.settings.context.* runtime context onto langsmith.metadata.* and sets span kinds, because the built-in rules are gated on ai.operationId which eve's span names never carry. LEARNEDConcrete things this session established. (1) eve reports the configured model as RuntimeIdentity.modelId, NOT runtime.model — I had read the wrong field, so the trace never learned its own model and every cost silently computed to $0 while tokens recorded fine. Classic invisible failure. (2) eve prefixes that id with the provider it routed through ('token-factory/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507') while the Token Factory catalog keys on the bare id, so the price lookup needs to peel prefixes. (3) createOpenAICompatible needs includeUsage: true or streamed turns report zero tokens forever. (4) LangSmith's OTLP exporter export() is a no-op unless LANGSMITH_TRACING is truthy — a key alone buys nothing, which is the worst kind of dead pipeline because it looks alive. (5) Declared subagents in eve inherit NOTHING — not tools, not hooks, not the disabled bash/glob/grep stubs — so the observe hook and every disabled tool had to be re-authored under the subagent dir (re-exports keep one implementation). (6) EveEvalJudgeConfig.model accepts a LanguageModel, so a Token Factory judge works inside eve evals, not just gateway ids. (7) `eve eval` takes --tag, not --tags. (8) Real product finding from the first eval run: given a complete brief in the opening message, Venus spent a whole turn interviewing anyway, because instructions §1 asked for a brief unconditionally. Fixed so she reads what she was given, confirms in a line, and fans out in the same response.
CURIOUSThe one reply-eval failure turned out to be a rule-ordering question rather than a model error: a vendor saying 'yes, that date is open, pricing depends on the package, let's hop on a call' was classified needs_info when the label said available. I promoted 'explicitly confirmed the date is open' above needs_info — the confirmed date is the headline fact a couple must hear as a win — and checked the two genuine needs_info cases don't state availability, so it isn't test-fitting. Worth revisiting whether that priority holds for other reply shapes. Open threads: eval:scout's judge samples only 4 vendors per category to stay affordable — is that enough signal? The Sentinel post mentions Snowglobe red-teaming, which I replaced with three adversarial cases in the reply set (injection, out-of-scope, malformed HTML) — a real simulation pass would be the next step. Also untested: what the rail looks like with 4 specialists running at once, and whether 5 concurrent SSE attachments hold up on a phone. And the documentation deliverable (the ASDAST 100 doc, three Nebius drafts judged, DeepSeek-V4-Pro won) is still paused and now needs updating for v18.

LEARNEDThe verification lesson is the sharp one: piping a build into grep does not verify anything — the exit status is grep's, and a build can fail with a message containing neither 'error' nor 'warn'. Added npm run verify (typecheck && next build && eve build && guard tests) so there is one exit-code-honest gate. Technical facts: disableTool() only covers eve's authored framework tools (ask_question, bash, glob, grep, load_skill, read_file, todo, web_fetch, web_search, write_file) — the built-in agent is not one, so shadowing it required authoring a real tool named agent that refuses and points at scout. eve 0.24.4 does not emit subagent.called on the parent stream despite the docs saying so; discover child sessions from each child's own trace via ctx.session.parent instead. Design lesson worth keeping: when a model has already broken a written rule, repeating the rule is not a control — record_vendor now REFUSES directory sources and foreign-domain emails, and the guards are unit-tested against 12 real rows from a production run (3 reject, 9 legitimate findings still pass, including gmail addresses and contact-form-only).
CURIOUSThe emailLooksForeign heuristic will false-reject a legitimate case eventually — a venue whose email sits on its parent company's domain, or a vendor using a booking platform address. The asymmetry justifies it (a false positive costs the couple a contact form; a false negative emails a stranger) but it is worth watching. Still unverified: whether a scout that receives rejected_directory_source recovers by opening the vendor's real site, or loops/drops the vendor — that is what the run in flight is testing. Also unverified: the two-pane layout visually, since I have no browser. Open: specialists take 20-40 steps and 400k-900k input tokens each; a tighter search-verify-record loop might halve that, and NEBIUS_SCOUT_MODEL is wired but unset (DeepSeek-V4-Flash is $0.14/$0.28 per Mtok vs Qwen's $0.20/$0.60). And durable eve sessions keep running and spending after the client disconnects — an abandoned eval session reached $5.18 across 18 agents on its own.

One bad decision made and corrected inside twenty minutes — the classifier briefly ran a model with a 13% schema failure rate in the production reply path. Told Jared plainly that I had said 'measured, not guessed' and that it was measured badly. Verification of the scout swap in flight.
LEARNEDThe night's sharpest lesson was methodological and it cost me a bad production change. npm run models:compare swept five models over the 15 labelled replies; DeepSeek-V4-Flash scored 15/15 at 16% less cost than the Qwen incumbent, so I switched the classifier to it. The very next run of the SAME fifteen cases through the real production path scored 11/15 with six schema failures. I built probe:schema to settle it: over 30 structured-output calls each, Qwen failed 0 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash failed 4 (13%) — 2x 'the model did not return a response', 2x 'could not parse the response'. So it was a real property, not rate limiting. The generalisable point: an accuracy sweep is structurally blind to schema failure, because a call that never returns an object is not a wrong answer, it is no answer, and averaged into a score it reads as a tie. Correctness of the content and reliability of the shape are different axes. Reverted the classifier, made models:compare run three rounds and rank on the WORST round, and kept probe:schema as a permanent check. Second finding worth keeping: Nemotron-3.5-Lightning is the cheapest model in the catalog per token ($0.06/$0.24) and was the most expensive per run and five times slower — price per token is not cost, output volume is.
CURIOUSThe scout still runs DeepSeek-V4-Flash despite that 13% structured-output failure, and I think that is right rather than sloppy: its findings reach the planner through record_vendor and the KV research store, never through its returned object, so a failed final report costs only the coverage note. Incremental recording was designed for truncation and turns out to cover schema failure for free — which is the strongest argument yet for the Sentinel pattern. But it is unverified: eval:scout on the DeepSeek scout is running against the 46/50 Qwen baseline. Open questions: does tool-calling reliability track structured-output reliability, or are they independent? Should probe:schema run against every role in CI? And the planner is still held constant on principle because no eval here measures prose — synthesis.eval.ts exists and has never been run, so there is a baseline sitting there uncollected.
WHY AIInferred. Jared's three questions were an audit: he wanted to know whether the claims matched the code. Two of the three answers were already true and provable from production data; the third exposed that everything except the judge ran on one model, which is exactly the prototype configuration his reference material starts from.

The cause was not only the model: the scout carried an outputSchema on defineAgent that I had added to 'guarantee' a structured return, and eve escalates a schema the model cannot produce into a failed child SESSION — so a formatting problem became a total loss, several specialists dying before they had searched once. The model also went straight for the final report instead of recording as it went, so there was no partial progress for the incremental design to protect. I had told Jared an hour earlier that a failed final report would cost 'the coverage note and nothing else'; that was wrong and I said so plainly. Reverted the scout to Qwen3-235B and DELETED the outputSchema entirely, because it was redundant: findings reach the planner through record_vendor and the KV research store that get_research reads, never through the child's return value. It bought nothing and could cost everything.

LEARNEDThe pattern across every fix tonight: when instructions are not enough, move the check into the tool — but only when the tool can actually perform it. Directory sources, foreign emails, missing locations and dead source URLs are all things a tool can verify, so they became refusals with guidance. Drive times are NOT — no geocoder, and search cannot answer them — so requiring one turned a guardrail into a seven-search death spiral. That distinction is the real lesson and it generalises well beyond this project. Second: leniency direction matters. The email guard is strict because a false positive costs a contact form and a false negative emails a stranger; the dead-source guard is lenient because a false positive throws away a real vendor and a false negative is caught by the eval anyway. Asymmetry should be reasoned about explicitly each time, not defaulted.

13:13HOME · AGENT-TOOLS — Jared asked for a vendor-neutral research brief on the state of the art in production AI-agent engineering as of August 2026, explicitly telling me his training data ends January 2026 and to assume anything he 'knows' is stale. Eight areas: (1) context engineering and what replaced naive RAG, (2) the evaluation stack including LLM-as-judge failure modes and debiasing, (3) agent reliability patterns including step-level compounding, durable execution, idempotency and critic loops, (4) long-term memory (episodic/semantic/procedural, consolidation, forgetting), (5) guardrails and prompt-injection defence including the 'lethal trifecta', (6) multi-agent orchestration and when it helps vs hurts, (7) cost and latency engineering, (8) anything genuinely new in 2026. He asked for URLs, dated sources, primary sources preferred, notes on where the field disagrees, and 2-3 actionable recommendations at the end. I ran this as a fan-out: five specialist subagents (evaluation, memory, multi-agent+cost, reliability, guardrails) plus my own sweep on context engineering and 2026-new items. Total ~450 tool calls; we exhausted the session WebSearch budget (200/200) partway through, so several agents finished on WebFetch and the arXiv API. Every agent came back with explicit UNVERIFIED flags, which was the right instinct. Highlights I found personally: Anthropic's context-management API primitives are now first-class (compact_20260112, clear_tool_uses_20250919, memory_20250818) with a cookbook dated 2026-03-20 showing peak context dropping 335K to ~170K; MCP spec revision 2026-07-28 went stateless-core with MRTR, header routing, CIMD auth and an extensions framework; Agent Skills became an open standard at agentskills.io with ~40 platforms including OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot, Mistral Vibe, Snowflake, Databricks; the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (Dec 2025) now stewards MCP, goose and AGENTS.md with 170+ members; Braintrust + Basis AI published 'behavior specs' (agentbehavior.dev, 2026-07-29) as an open standard for supervising long-horizon agents; and OpenAI Evals is being sunset (read-only 2026-10-31, shutdown 2026-11-30) which is the single most actionable operational item in the whole brief. The most interesting genuine disagreements I surfaced: compaction vs cache preservation (louisbouchard.ai 2026-08-18 says full history with prompt caching beats summarisation on cost, latency and recall; arXiv 2606.10209 measures pruning+summarisation at 91.6% vs 71.0% full-history completion — both can't be right in general); grep/agentic search vs vector search vs GraphRAG (Anthropic dropped vectors from Claude Code, arXiv 2605.05242 Direct Corpus Interaction beats dense baselines, LlamaIndex's 2026-01-13 benchmark shows filesystem wins small and RAG wins at scale, and the AI Engineer 2026 Q1 report claims GraphRAG gives 3x); multi-agent +90.2% (Anthropic, uncontrolled compute) vs arXiv 2604.02460 showing single-agent matches or beats multi-agent at equal thinking-token budget; and Anthropic saying auto mode has 'pretty much mitigated every attack' (720/720 held-out injections blocked) versus Johann Rehberger breaking it at ~80% thirteen days after GA. The number that reframed the whole brief for me: METR's 50% time horizon is now measured in hours (Opus 4.5 at 320 min, Opus 4.6 reported ~12h) but the 80% horizon is roughly an hour, and the 99% horizon is not measurable at all with existing task suites. Everything in reliability engineering exists to close that gap outside the model.
OUTCOMEShipped. Delivered a dense eight-section brief with roughly 150 dated, URL-cited sources, explicit disagreement callouts, explicit unverified-claim flags, and three actionable recommendations (treat the 80% time horizon as the design constraint and engineer reversibility rather than accuracy; calibrate LLM judges with held-out TPR/TNR splits and Rogan-Gladen correction before trusting any eval number; cut a lethal-trifecta leg at the infrastructure layer since every 2026 bypass defeated an allowlist rather than a classifier). Also flagged the OpenAI Evals sunset as time-sensitive. Waste to be honest about: ~15 no-op `date` polling calls while waiting on subagents, and the exhausted search budget meant three of five agents finished degraded. The brief is still strong because every agent hedged with WebFetch and the arXiv API, and because I did parallel hedge fetches on the sections most likely to come back thin (I fetched Anthropic's managed-agents, harness-design, prompt-caching and demystifying-evals posts myself, plus tau-bench, HAL, Harbor, agentskills.io and the MCP 2026-07-28 spec).
LEARNEDJared learned (or will learn when he reads the brief): that his January-2026 mental model is materially stale on at least six fronts — context management is now a first-class API surface rather than a client-side hack; the eval tooling he might reach for (OpenAI Evals) is being shut down in November; SWE-bench Verified was retired by OpenAI in Feb 2026 after an audit found 59.4% of hard tasks flawed; benchmark hygiene (broken tasks, infrastructure noise worth ~6pp, eval-awareness where models go find the answer key) is now a bigger story than benchmark scores; the multi-agent debate resolved not by one side winning but by everyone converging on 'fan out on reads, never on writes'; and prompt injection defence moved decisively from model-layer to capability-scoping and information-flow control, with argument-level provenance (PACT) beating message-level taint by 8-16 points at equal security. I also learned some things about my own process: fanning out five subagents on a shared WebSearch budget starved the later ones — the memory, eval and reliability agents all reported hitting the 200-call cap and finishing on WebFetch. Next time I should either raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION up front or stagger the launches. Also: I wasted maybe fifteen tool calls polling `date` while waiting for subagents instead of doing useful hedge research. The Monitor tool with a sleep loop is the right pattern but I kept short-circuiting it.
CURIOUSOpen threads worth returning to: (1) the compaction-vs-full-history question is genuinely unresolved and is exactly the kind of thing Jared could measure on his own agents cheaply — what does his actual cache hit rate look like, and does compaction ever pay for itself at his scale? (2) METR's Opus 4.6 50% horizon is reported as both ~12h and 14.5h and I could not extract the authoritative value from METR's live chart; someone should just read the chart. (3) Nobody has run the decisive multi-agent experiment — a compute-normalised comparison on a genuinely breadth-first research task, which is precisely the workload where Anthropic's +90.2% was measured. (4) 'Undo over approve' is widely advocated (Gartner, the AgentRunner paper) but there is no controlled study comparing it to approval gates. (5) CaMeL has been out for 17 months and there is still no identifiable production deployment — why? (6) Whether 'behavior specs' (.agents/behaviors/BEHAVIOR.md) actually gets adopted the way SKILL.md did, or whether it's a vendor standard that dies. (7) I did not verify anything about ISO 42001 agent-specific developments in 2026 — a real gap. (8) Jared didn't say what this brief is FOR — interview prep, a talk, a build decision? The framing would change what I'd emphasise.
WHY AIInferred: this is a breadth problem with a hard recency constraint — eight technical domains, a seven-month gap between Jared's mental model and the present, and a requirement for dated primary sources. Doing this by hand would be days of reading. The fan-out to five parallel specialist agents is the specific thing that makes it tractable in twenty minutes, and it is not something Jared could do alone at all. He was also explicit that he wanted to be corrected rather than confirmed ('assume anything I know may be outdated'), which is a task shape that suits an agent with live web access much better than a search engine.

LEARNEDeve protocol detail that cost real time: createActionResultEvent attaches an error object to a REJECTED action result, not only a failed one, because buildActionResultError falls back to {code:'ACTION_RESULT_FAILED', message: formatActionResultOutput(output)} and never returns undefined. Any code that tests `data.error` before `data.status` will silently reclassify every approval-gate denial as a failure. Corollary for the soft-failure case: normalizeActionResultOutcome returns status 'completed' with NO error for a tool that reports {status:'search_failed'} in its payload — so a soft failure has neither an exception nor an error field, which is exactly why it was invisible. The generalisable lesson, which is now the thesis of the engineering log: a test that exercises a pure function while nothing exercises its consumer will let a correct table and an incorrect reading of it ship together. Both of my failed fixes were tested one level below the defect. Also: scanning broadly for a pattern (every `status:` literal in agent/lib) produces false positives that train the reader to add junk to the taxonomy. Precision in a completeness check matters as much as coverage.
CURIOUSWhether the record_vendor conservatism is the right default. I made an unrecognised status NOT count as a recorded vendor, on the reasoning that a visible duplicate re-run beats a silent gap in the plan — but that asymmetry is a judgment call and I documented it rather than measured it. Also still unmeasured: whether dry_run and sent_to_test_inbox belong in SUCCESS_STATUSES. I argued yes (the deployment mode decided it, not the input; the /outreach audit answers 'did it actually go') but a reviewer could reasonably call a dry run a non-send. And the pending items from before this round are untouched: the batched-search speed claim is still unverified against a real run, the cross-session vendor knowledge layer is still scaffolding at ~/venus-graph, judge calibration (TPR/TNR against human labels) is still named-but-not-done, and every eval score is still a single run rather than pass^k.

LEARNEDVerified a real user-facing failure mode in the AI SDK part model: `state === "output-available"` answers whether a tool call RETURNED, never whether it SUCCEEDED. Any tool that reports refusal or failure in its return payload — which is the whole design of this codebase — renders as success under that test. The part's state answers 'did it finish'; its output answers 'what happened'. Same distinction as actionOutcome vs the runtime's exception view. Measurement technique worth reusing: to get an honest before/after on bundle size, don't read the Next build table (Next 16 doesn't print one here). Start the production server, curl the route, regex the /_next/static/chunks/*.js out of the returned HTML, and gzip each file. That is exactly what the browser fetches, it works identically against localhost and production, and it survives git stash for a true A/B. toLocaleString without an explicit timeZone is a guaranteed SSR hydration mismatch on Vercel (server UTC, client local). suppressHydrationWarning on the wrapping element is the correct fix when the client value is the one you want.

And whether costFor having zero assertions in npm run verify should be closed now that agentCost is the single reading — the test surface finally exists.

LEARNEDSeveral things that came from testing rather than reading. 1. The research note ranked 'missing defer=True fires synthesis on the first specialist to finish' as the top risk in this design. I wrote a test to prove it and the test FAILED to reproduce it — every Send to a single node lands in the same LangGraph superstep, so synthesis runs once with all findings whether or not defer is set. What defer actually protects is a fan-in whose branches have DIFFERENT DEPTHS: the moment any specialist grows a second node, synthesis runs twice and the first run sees partial findings, silently. Rewrote the test to demonstrate that instead, including the failing case. This matters because the corpus path would be exactly such a second node. 2. directoryHost matched its patterns as substrings of the whole URL, so 'wedding.com' matched luxewedding.com and 'brides.com' matched sarahbrides.com — real vendors' own domains silently discarded, with no way for a scout to appeal a guard. A share link in a query string did the same. Host-anchoring alone does NOT fix it (luxewedding.com still contains wedding.com in the host); it needs label-boundary matching. Fixed in BOTH arms, because fixing only Python would fork the guards and a benchmark whose arms enforce different rules measures the rules. Proved the 9 new regression cases fail on the old code before trusting them: 4 failed. 3. SummarizationMiddleware(trigger=('fraction', 0.85)) raises at graph construction for any model reached through a custom base_url — LangChain needs a model-profile registry entry it does not have for Nebius. The context window was already in the price table, so an absolute ('tokens', N) threshold works without the registry. 4. The first live run crashed and reported $0.00 spent — while the planner call had already completed and been billed. That is precisely the failure usage.py's docstring claims to prevent (Sentinel: 'tokens burned before a crash were still billed'). invoke() raising discards the state and every finished node with it. Added a run-scoped ledger nodes write to on their way through.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash was blamed for 10/10 scout failures, but the diagnosed cause was the schema (the constraint-tax paper says tool-calling + JSON-Schema together makes models stop invoking tools entirely), and the schema is gone. The reversal to Qwen therefore rests on an experiment whose confound has since been removed. Jared did not pick this lever when offered, so it stays open. Also open: whether the batched search actually moves the 166s/220s number. The data to measure it is already captured (TraceEntry.dt, rendered per row but never aggregated) and nothing aggregates thinking-time vs tool-time yet. And: is the LangGraph A/B honest given Approach B is script-driven with no durable background execution? eve gives durable sessions, resume and cron for free. I put that in the README as a stated limit rather than something to engineer around, but it means the comparison measures orchestration quality, not production-readiness.

No 'What we learned' or 'Gotchas' section exists; lessons instead arrive as clipped one-sentence-per-line prose ('That cost is fine.' / 'The wait is not.' / 'This is not magic acceleration.'). OUTCOMEAnswered: no, it was not the projects. Wrote a sourced neighborhood history distinguishing City Point private 1939 apartments from Southie's BHA developments.
LEARNED25 Lennon Court was not Boston Housing Authority public housing. It is a 42-unit private brick courtyard apartment complex built in 1939 in City Point (East Side of South Boston), converted to condos in 1978. The visual similarity to 1930s PWA public housing (3-story brick walk-ups around a courtyard) plus the 1939 date is why it can look like 'the projects.' Southie's actual family public housing was: Mary Ellen McCormack / Old Harbor Village (opened 1938, ~1,016 units, 30 acres near Andrew Square / Moakley Park), Old Colony (1940, now Anne M. Lynch Homes, East 9th), and West Broadway / D Street (1949). Foley Apartments at 199 H Street is BHA elderly housing from 1963, a few blocks west of Lennon Court, not family projects. City Point was historically the more desirable eastern tip of Southie (Castle Island, yacht clubs, Marine Park) versus the Lower End (A–F streets) and the public-housing superblocks. Nearby Twomey Court (1946, 66 units) converted in the same 1978 condo wave.
CURIOUSWho built Lennon Court in 1939 (private developer vs FHA-financed garden apartments) and who the street is named for. What sat on the Columbia Road / M Street block before 1939 (1910 Bromley atlas exists at Leventhal). Deed trail of the 1978 master deed at Suffolk Registry.
WHY AILocal history / property-history research across Redfin, BHA lists, preservation studies, and Southie housing literature — faster to have an agent pull and synthesize than to do it by hand.

Grok theming docs: fullscreen TUI paints its own truecolor theme and ignores the terminal palette; minimal mode is the exception and uses Ghostty's 16-color ANSI. Claude Code's dark theme is also its own RGB; dark-ansi/light-ansi would inherit Ghostty. Grok built-ins: GrokNight, GrokDay, TokyoNight, RosePineMoon, OscuraMidnight — no Everforest. LEARNEDGhostty theme does not paint Grok fullscreen or Claude Code dark. Grok auto = GrokNight/GrokDay. Claude is hardcoded dark. Only shell, git/ls, Grok --minimal, and Claude ansi themes inherit the terminal palette. Grok /theme and Claude /theme are the real color controls for those apps. RosePineMoon is Grok's closest easy-on-eyes built-in.
CURIOUSWhether he wants Grok switched to RosePineMoon (or auto_dark_theme) and Claude to dark-ansi so Everforest actually shows through, or a custom Claude theme that matches Everforest.

07:39MACBOOK AIR M3 — Jared asked: 'at what temperatrure does macbook air start to thermal throttle mine is 132f right now and feels slow'. He is on this machine: 13-inch MacBook Air M3 (Mac15,12), 16 GB RAM, macOS 27.0, Stats.app with Fahrenheit units (so 132F is almost certainly the Stats CPU/sensor reading, not a kitchen thermometer on the case). I checked live: CPU ~76% idle, load 2.33/2.68/3.27, pmset reports no thermal/performance warning, ~901 processes, PhysMem 15G used / 551M unused with ~5 GB in the compressor and ~450 MB swap used (31k swapouts). Browsers/WebKit/Chrome/Brave/Safari/Grok Bot/Proton Mail together ~75 procs / ~3.7 GB RSS. Battery 441 cycles, FullChargeCapacity 3721 vs Design 4563 (~82%).
OUTCOMEAnswered: 132F is not throttle territory. Pointed at memory pressure as the more likely cause of feeling slow. No config change.
LEARNEDMacBook Air (fanless Apple Silicon) does not throttle at chassis-warm 132F. Chip die throttle is around 95-100C / 203-212F; M3 Air stress tests peaked ~114C then settled ~100C. 132F is 55.6C — normal/cool die temp. macOS thermal pressure (Nominal/Fair/Serious/Critical) is the real signal; this Mac had no thermal warning. Slowness at 132F on a 16GB M3 Air is much more likely RAM compression/swap than heat.
CURIOUSWhat was the actual Stats sensor (CPU die vs proximity vs GPU)? Was the lid closed / on a blanket? Why so many WebKit + Chrome + Brave + Safari + Grok Bot at once on 16GB.
WHY AIQuick factual + live machine check; easier than looking up M3 Air throttle curves and converting F/C while the machine feels slow. Inference.

Debugger message panic. OS version 26A428, Darwin Kernel 27.0.0 (Tue Aug 11 2026) RELEASE_ARM64_T8122 (M4). Panicked task watchdogd pid 588. Sleep/Wake timestamps were 0. Post-boot kexts included usb.cdc, usb.cdc.ecm, usb.cdc.acm, usb.realtek8153patcher, AppleUSBHostBillboardDevice, UVCService, AppleUSBAudio, USB mass storage. Live IORegistry on this Mac shows the exact named object: CDC Communications Control as IOUSBHostInterface on Realtek 'USB 10/100/1000 LAN' idVendor 3034 idProduct 33107 (RTL8153), sitting under a TB4CDOCK Thunderbolt 4 dock (idVendor 5296) plus Logitech BRIO, Magic Keyboard, USB hubs. OUTCOMEExplained the panic. No code change. Machine is up now with the same Realtek CDC interface enumerated (busy 0).

WHY AIInference: kernel panic dump is unreadable without mapping IOKit names to the actual USB tree; faster to have the log decoded than to stare at hex.

Measured: race n=4 same weights 17.5s Nebius vs 53.7s Gateway (3.1×); 13×13 external 98 turns / 996s / 2.44M tokens / $4.40; prompt-trim of get_state-first and re-verify-before-submit cut a generated 5×5 from ~420s to 153s; fast non-reasoning model did 3×3 in 2.5s but 1/4 on the full set. OUTCOMENo code. Honest speed answer: not way faster as a drop-in solver; yes faster as candidate/slot/submit router in front of Token Factory and the existing engine.
LEARNEDJev cannot generate crossword answers from clues, so it cannot replace V4 Pro as the solver. Where it is actually faster is indexed decisions the LLM currently burns a full turn on: pick a slot, pick among wordlist/LLM candidates, submit vs continue, which slot to clear. That is the Browser Use pattern applied to fill_slot. On already-short 2–5 turn 5×5 solves, an extra Jev RTT is not 'way faster'. On the 13×13, Jev+wordlist Choice could skip many ~10s Pro turns if most entries are dictionary words that fit the pattern.

WHY AIInference: he wanted the Jev research from the previous turn mapped onto a project he already measured, faster than re-reading grok.md and TypeSafe primitives himself.

T490 Intel UHD 620 cannot encode 2560x1600/1664 at 60 fps (measured ~35 fps HEVC); 1080p60 HEVC at ~50 Mbps is the 60fps path. YUV 4:4:4 is the crisp-text feature but this Sunshine host does not advertise 444 (codec mask 257) and software 444 would kill the iGPU. 150 Mbps on Wi-Fi plus H.264 at panel-native res caused queue overflow and audio drops.

16:24DEEPGRAM-VOICE-AGENT — Mic-bug investigation wrapped while Jared was testing the app live. Mid-turn he sent 'it works' — he had clicked the orb in one of my open test windows and the app transcribed and answered him. Refined root cause of the original complaint ('when i use the microphone it doesn't capture my voice'): Chrome's out-of-process audio service on this Mac (macOS 27.0 26A428 + Chrome 153.0.8010.53) can take ~10-15s to deliver the FIRST mic capture in a fresh Chrome session. My earlier probes raced getUserMedia at 9s and read 'slow' as 'hung' — misdiagnosis. Evidence chain: ffmpeg recorded the mic fine at OS level (mean -37dB, max -19.7dB); with --disable-features=AudioServiceOutOfProcess capture initialized fast; a no-flag fresh instance eventually captured at ~12s and literally transcribed Jared asking 'Hey. Do I have to click the stop button on the microphone, or can I just leave it live?' Shipped two fixes: 811365f (getUserMedia bounded with explanatory error; hook surfaces real error text) and 34304ed (new 'Starting mic' status shown immediately on orb click, bound raised to 25s, cancel-safe start via token guard). Verified live on prod: orb click -> 'Starting mic' at 0.0s -> 'Listening' at 3.75s.
OUTCOMETwo commits pushed and deployed (811365f, 34304ed); prod verified 'Starting mic' -> 'Listening'. Two test Chrome windows left open on the desktop for Jared (one flagged fast-mic instance, one plain) — his call to close. User-confirmed working ('it works').
LEARNEDChrome on this machine cold-starts mic capture slowly (~4-15s); a bounded probe that's too short makes a slow subsystem look hung. --disable-features=AudioServiceOutOfProcess is the fast path. OS-level mic verification via ffmpeg avfoundation takes 30 seconds and splits OS-vs-browser cleanly. A voice app should show a distinct 'starting' state — silent waits read as broken.
CURIOUSDoes Jared's own normal Chrome work now with patience (or does it need the flag / a launcher)? Does the cold-start reproduce after a Chrome update or a machine reboot, or is it per-session? Would a warmed-up Chrome (first capture primed) make every later capture instant for him?
WHY AIInference: the bug lived at the boundary of browser/OS behavior that's only diagnosable by driving Chrome and probing live state — exactly what an agent can do while Jared keeps using the app.

LEARNEDPerceived 'voice lag' in a turn-based voice pipeline = STT + LLM + TTS are sequential round trips; text can render as soon as the LLM answers, so if you want text and voice together you must gate the text on audio start, not on chat return. LEARNEDOn iOS Safari, when getUserMedia is active the audio session is play-and-record which routes output to the earpiece. A standalone Audio element plays through the default route (earpiece). LEARNEDOn this Mac the default input was Jared's AirPods Max over Bluetooth at 24 kHz, input volume 53, not muted. A short ffmpeg avfoundation capture from device index 3 was not silent: mean about -33.9 dB, peak -9.1 dB. The app speech threshold is RMS 0.02, about -34 dBFS, so cabin noise sits near the trigger and speech peaks clear it. Browser permission is a separate hop from the OS input.
WHY AIHe could not tell from the plane whether the headset mic was live. A short level probe on the actual input device answers that without guessing.

LEARNEDA moving level bar is not a sent turn. Cabin noise sits on a fixed 0.02 RMS cutoff, so the utterance never closes. Speech has to be a rise above the recent noise floor, with a hard close around 8 seconds.
WHY AIThe send path was a silence detector, and a plane never goes silent.

08:44DEEPGRAM-VOICE-AGENT — Jared is on a plane and asked to triple-check the mic, because it still does not pick up what he says, and for a way to test it.

LEARNEDOnce the cabin floor adapts, speech at 1.6x that floor never opens a 2.6x gate, so the recorder never starts. A rolling buffer plus an explicit Send is what actually ships the clip. Browser noise suppression and auto gain flatten that rise further.
WHY AIThe moving level bar was not a sent turn, and only a forced send proves the path on a plane.

S2871 uses the TypeScript type checker on zero-arg .sort() and, for string arrays, asks for localeCompare. S8786 parses the regex with regexpp and calls the scslre library, and only reports when the result is super-linear and not exponential. S9383 is typescript-eslint no-floating-promises wrapped by Sonar. S7773 is the unicorn eslint rule prefer-number-properties. S5850 walks the regex AST for anchor/alternation precedence. The three dog-run tssecurity findings (S5145 log injection, S8476 client-side request forgery, S7044 API traversal) are all in scripts/e2e-booking.ts, a local e2e script whose header says it is local-only; line 49 is fetch(`${BASE}${path}`) with path a function parameter. SonarJS does contain skills, but they are for the engineers who write the analyzer: .claude/skills/new-rule scaffolds a visitor, rule-implementation traces context.report() for false positives, and peach-check triages the internal Peach Main Analysis corpus (peachee-js) before a release. Those skills do not run on a customer's repo. AI CodeFix, Remediation Agent, and Hunter Agent are the products that call an LLM; they did not produce these findings. Messages are identical canned strings, not prose about pollen or menus. Two places the existing overview over-reads the analyzer: SchedulePicker slots are zero-padded 06:00–20:00, so default string sort already orders them and the '10:00 before 9:00' example is not this file; S8786 is polynomial super-linear by design, not the exponential 'catastrophic backtrack / hung request' story. train247 is private; the issues API returned 0, so those 76 were not re-listed. 11:52DHANUNJAY-DIVI__NOOP · WHOOP — Jared asked to review the forked offline WHOOP repo https://github.com/jaredwerba/Dhanunjay-Divi__Noop and https://developer.whoop.com/docs/introduction, then create a technical plan for an offline dog movement tracker using a WHOOP 5.0MG as the sensor and Noop as the existing software layer. LEARNEDOfficial WHOOP developer API is OAuth cloud summaries (cycle, recovery, sleep, workout, profile, body) plus webhooks. It does not supply raw IMU or an offline device path. Medical-grade MG data is not in that API. Noop's Whoop5RawImu decodes a 1-second, 100 Hz, 6-axis historical IMU buffer (accel 1/4096 g/LSB, gyro ±2000 dps), validated on a WHOOP 5.0 at firmware 50.40.1.0 across 1423 buffers. The live raw-IMU command acks and does not stream. MG and 5.0 share DeviceFamily.whoop5 framing; Whoop5Variant separates hardware. ECG is MG-only and needs finger contact on the clasp. ImuFeatureExtractor's cadence band is human (1.2–3.5 Hz). WHOOP 5/MG support in Noop is experimental. License is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. macOS cannot complete the 5/MG authenticated bond; the collector is a phone.
CURIOUSHow long a WHOOP MG retains continuous 100 Hz IMU frames while the phone is away. Whether an MG matches the 5.0 gravity-shell validation. Whether membership lapse stops strap recording or only the official app. Whether chest-harness PPG can see canine heart rate through coat. What cadence band fits small, medium, and large dogs.
WHY AIInference: the repo is large and the official docs describe a different system than the local BLE layer. Jared asked for a review plus an architecture he can execute.

11:53WHOOP-ARCHIVE · NOOP — Jared asked how to use an old WHOOP 5.0/MG sensor as a very basic dog activity tracker: steps, movement, distance only, no HR. He already has an offline client that can read the strap. He asked for research on what the sensor can do and a weekend-project plan.
OUTCOMEGave a weekend plan: Saturday prove the counter on a known human walk via the client's CSV, then collar-mount and calibrate stride on a measured loop; Sunday daily BLE history pull and a one-page log of steps, active minutes, estimated km, still/walk/run. Explicitly not a GPS or live-location tracker.
LEARNEDWHOOP 5.0/MG has no onboard GPS. Connected GPS is the phone during a started workout. Motion is a TDK ICM-45686 6-axis IMU with an on-chip APEX pedometer (step count, cadence, walk/run/unknown). Pod is 34.7x24x10.6 mm, ~26.5 g, IP68 10 m, ~14 day battery. 5.0 vs MG: serial prefix 5AG vs 5AM; MG only adds ECG. NOOP (local archive at /Users/jkw/whoop-archive/repos/ryanbr__noop) already decodes WHOOP 5 historical layout-18: step_motion_counter at byte 57 (u16 cumulative), cadence at 59, activity_class at 63 (0 still/1 walk/2 run), gravity xyz at 45/49/53, dyn accel at 41. Stored as stepSample and gravitySample; raw CSV export exists. Protocol notes say the counter is not proven equal to the official app total and rollover is unresolved. Distance must be stride x steps, calibrated per dog. Not a location tracker.
CURIOUSWhether Jared's offline client is NOOP or a different one, and whether a collar-mounted walk test actually moves byte 57. If the hardware counter is dead on a dog neck, the fallback is a 1 Hz gravity peak detector.
WHY AINeeded cross-check of WHOOP hardware specs, the ICM-45686 pedometer, and the local NOOP protocol docs so the plan used fields the client already stores instead of inventing a BLE stack.
TAGSLEARNING · LIFE · CODE

Jenkins 2018 PLOS and Zhang 2022 Scientific Reports are limb IMUs; public Jenkins file is step timing, Zhang data is on request. Royal Society Open Science 2024 (10.1098/rsos.240119, Dryad 10.5061/dryad.m0cfxppbs) publishes collar dynamic vector means: lie 0.02 g, sit 0.08 g, stand 0.13 g, walk 0.26 g, trot 0.59 g. LEARNEDWHOOP support and community staff: the pod stores up to 14 days of unsynced data locally; the app shows data catching up after Bluetooth returns. That is not a published flash size, and it is not proof that every 100 Hz IMU second lasts 14 days. Staff (27 May 2025 and 10 Apr 2026): the official app can hold Bluetooth only while it remains in the background; a force-quit pauses sync until reopen. Within about 30 feet it syncs over BLE; out of range it waits and does not drain itself hunting the phone. GitHub topic whoop, most stars, checked 2026-10-05: OpenStrap/edge, about 658 stars and 118 forks, Dart/Flutter, WHOOP 4/5/MG, https://github.com/OpenStrap/edge. Most forks among strap clients is johnmiddleton12/wearable (OpenWhoop), about 157 forks and 312 stars, WHOOP 4.0 only. OpenStrap README: Android uses a foreground service, 15-minute watchdog, CompanionDeviceManager. iOS uses a background processing task, a light refresh task, and a separate restore Bluetooth central that can relaunch when the band reconnects. They say iOS background sync is best-effort: usually, not always, because Apple does not give third-party apps a real background service. History batches need an 8-byte token echoed back or the band resends forever; they save locally before that ack. Nobody keeps a GATT session after the user swipes the app away. Dog Pace totals still live only in process RAM.

19:19DOG-PACE — Jared asked about the Dog Pace screen itself: dog size Small / Large / Custom, his dog is an English bulldog about 55 lb, and what Walk onset means. No code change.
OUTCOMEExplained the two controls. Did not change the preset or the threshold.
LEARNEDDog size only sets meters per peak. Small is 0.37 m (Kim 2011, dogs under 10 kg). Large is 0.83 m (same paper, dogs over 25 kg, longer-legged). Custom leaves the slider. A 55 lb bulldog is about 25 kg, on the Large weight line, but 0.83 m is expected to read long on a short-limbed bulldog. Walk onset is the 1-second mean of |acceleration − 1 g|, default (0.13+0.26)/2 = 0.195 g, shown as 0.20 g. At or below it the label stays lie/sit/stand and peaks do not count. Above it the label is Walking until the trot cut. Leave 0.20 g until a real walk looks wrong. Calibrate meters with one measured walk: meters per peak = measured meters / peak count.
CURIOUSWhat meters-per-peak a measured bulldog walk actually produces, versus 0.83.
WHY AIInference: he was looking at the live controls and wanted the meaning of the labels for this specific dog, not a code change.

21:24DOG-VV00P3 · ASHERLC__WHOOP-BLE-SWIFT — Jared asked: "is all sensor data being saved to the whoop sensor? if the app is disconnected, will the sensor send the data to the app?" About VV00P and the WHOOP 5.0 MG named JKW. No code change.
OUTCOMEAnswered from the connect path in StrapSession and WhoopBleClient.requestStoredMotion, plus WHOOP's support claim. Nothing shipped.
LEARNEDThe strap records its own buffer. WHOOP support says the device stores up to 14 days of unsynced data and their app syncs it over Bluetooth when reconnected (support article Why is my WHOOP Catching Up). VV00P does not write onto the sensor. On Connect it sends SEND_HISTORICAL_DATA 0x16 with [0x00] once and does not ack, so it does not tell the strap to drop records. The phone diary is one SQLite row per strap second: resting or moving, peaks, distance. Heart rate, temperature, ECG, blood pressure, and raw 100 Hz samples are not stored by this app. A disconnected app receives nothing until the next Connect. A full gap arriving in one unacked request is unproven. The official WHOOP app can trim the buffer if it syncs first.
CURIOUSWhether one reconnect after a long gap delivers every stored motion second, since the historical chunk is left unacked. How many hours of 100 Hz motion this MG actually retains.
WHY AIInferred: Jared wanted the strap's own memory and this app's catch-up behavior explained before he trusts a disconnect.
TAGSCODE · LEARNING

OUTCOMEResearch only. Did not touch Dog-VV00P3 sources because he is mid-build and pushing. Recommendation: do not buy Fi/Tractive/Whistle, T1000-E, or WisMesh Tag as the sensor. If he wants a sealed weekend prototype, Bangle.js 2 proves GPS+buzz+BLE and fails the two-week-with-GPS bar. If he wants the actual pod, XIAO nRF52840 Sense + u-blox M10 module (not the 40 mm breakout) + DRV2605L, GPS duty-cycled, antenna at the crown of the neck.
LEARNEDLocal checkout is /Users/jkw/Dog-VV00P3 (GitHub jaredwerba/Dog-VV00P). Research notes already say the WHOOP 5.0/MG is a BLE activity logger only: 34.7x24x10.6 mm, ~26.5 g, IP68, ~14 day battery, ICM-45686 IMU, TI DRV2625 haptic, no GPS chip. Connected GPS is the phone. No sealed product matches GPS + commandable haptic + 2-week battery + BLE you can flash in a WHOOP-sized pod. Closest sealed hackable object is Espruino Bangle.js 2 (nRF52840, AT6558 GPS, KX022 accel, vibration motor, IP67 everyday-not-swim, 175 mAh, GPS at 26 mA so continuous positioning is under a day; shop price about £83). Best DIY collar brain is Seeed XIAO nRF52840 Sense (21x17.8 mm, LSM6DS3TR-C, BLE, <5 uA sleep, Li-ion charger) plus a u-blox M10 (SparkFun MAX-M10S breakout is $45.95 and needs an antenna; SAM-M10Q chip-antenna breakout is $51.50 and 40.6 mm square, too wide as a breakout) plus Adafruit DRV2605L for the buzz. Credit-card trackers fail the form factor: RAK WisMesh Tag is $39, 92x59x7.5 mm, IP66, 1000 mAh, AT6558R, LIS2DH, BLE+LoRa, no haptic. Seeed T1000-E is 85x55x6.5 mm, 32 g, IP65, 700 mAh, buzzer, accel unused by Meshtastic, up to ~2 days. LIA (JGAguado) is the closest open collar: ESP32-S3, SX1262, SAM-M10Q, LSM6DSOX, waterproof enclosure, 18650 or 1000 mAh pouch, LoRa-first, no confirmed haptic. Loko is 30x23 mm / 12 g LoRa GPS with no IMU and no buzz. Fi Series 3 hits size and battery (high activity up to 2 weeks) only via LTE-M subscription and a closed app. OpenCollar is a cattle collar, ~1.2 kg target, not a dog. Battery arithmetic from published M10 tracking current (~8-10 mA): 1000 mAh continuous is about 4 days; a 10% duty cycle (30 s fix every 5 min) is what makes two weeks possible. Existing StrapSession speaks WHOOP GATT, so none of these pair into the current app.
CURIOUSWhether VV00P v3 must stay BLE-to-the-phone (yard/room sync, like the WHOOP logger) or must answer where-is-the-dog outside BLE range. That fork decides XIAO+M10 versus a LoRa collar (LIA). Also whether he will accept a printed shell or wants a sealed watch body this weekend.

Seeed warns not to drive P0.14 high while charging. 3V3 rail is rated 200 mA. Distance is haversine when the fix is valid, stride times the onboard step counter otherwise, never both. 07:59DOG-VV00P3 · WHOOPBLE · NOOP — Jared asked: "when noop was connected one of the features was that the bluetooth dialogue popped up and the app asked to find nearby bluetooth devices. the biggest problem right now is that the connection closes if the app is idle. is there any way to fix that by connecting the sensor to the iphone once and it always being connected?" This is Max Werba at /Users/jkw/Dog-VV00P3, one WHOOP strap. He remembers Noop (ryanbr/noop, which he ran as Dog-VV00P2) showing a system Bluetooth sheet and wants the strap to stay linked when the phone is idle.
OUTCOMEAnswered. No code change. The always-on session is still not built.
LEARNEDThat sheet is iOS Bluetooth permission, fired the first time an app creates a CBCentralManager. Noop's NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription explains the strap. The permission does not pin the radio. A WHOOP link is owned by one app's central. The official app holds it in the background and loses it on a force-quit. VV00P already declares bluetooth-central. WhoopBLE creates the central with restore id com.dofek.whoop-ble-central and sets autoReconnect after connect, but only when Connect runs inside StrapSession. VV00PApp does not create the central at launch, so iOS cannot restore a jettisoned process. Scene background only flushes the diary; it does not call disconnect. The handshake timeout is 10 seconds and applies during connecting, discovering, and subscribing, not to an already streaming idle link. A durable fix is launch-time restoration plus a saved peripheral UUID and notify-on-connect. It still cannot survive a force-quit, a reboot, or the official WHOOP app taking the strap.
CURIOUSHe may want that background restore built next. He has not said to build it. Whether his idle drop is a lock-screen suspend or a force-quit is still his observation, not a log from this turn.
WHY AIInferred: he wanted the iOS Bluetooth limit checked against this app and Noop before trying to pair the strap in Settings.

LEARNEDVV00P is a local diary: resting/moving, stride distance, strain, 30-minute goal, day history, buzz in BLE range, a 10-second moving alert that only fires while the phone is connected. It has no map, geofence, live find, route, or home base. Competitors that still work are Fi (LTE-M, WiFi home zone, escape alert, activity/sleep, advertised lick/scratch/bark/eat, subscription, US) and Tractive (LIVE 2-3s, virtual fences, location history, activity/sleep/scratching/vitals, 175+ countries, subscription). Whistle was shut down 31 Aug 2025 after Tractive bought it. FindMyCat is the open rival: GPS+LTE, UWB precise find, HomeStation tether, sound, claimed 6-month battery, still a cloud. LIA is LoRa GPS with no subscription and no phone-from-the-park unless a mesh node exists. A different sensor only adds a finder if the radio is LTE, LoRa-plus-gateway, or UWB-while-nearby. GNSS alone adds a route log, not a lost-dog alert.
CURIOUSWhether he wants a finder or a better diary. That choice is the sensor.
WHY AIThe gap is product-shaped, not a missing screen in ContentView. Needed current competitor pages so Whistle was not recommended as a living product.

LEARNEDAn AirTag is not interoperable with VV00P. Apple has no public Find My location API. The location is decrypted only on his signed-in devices. A third-party app cannot read an AirTag, cannot command it, and cannot add GPS, a mic, or a motor to it. The only DIY path that joins the crowd network is OpenHaystack, which is a beacon he builds, not a tap into a real AirTag. Power: WHOOP 5/MG is a sealed LiPo charged by the Battery Pack, no user cell. AirTag is one CR2032, more than a year, no charge port. A DIY collar is one rechargeable LiPo, 500 to 1000 mAh, charged over USB-C on the XIAO, not a coin cell.
CURIOUSWhether a CR2032 beacon on the same collar as the LiPo pod is worth the extra case, given he already rejected subscriptions and wants GPS plus a mic plus a buzz.
WHY AIThe AirTag question is a protocol lock, not a product preference. Needed Apple's own position, not a shop page.

OUTCOMERead the five files and reported them. Did not copy the notes into the app, did not change stride, did not implement R18.
LEARNEDHermes concluded the pod can be a collar activity logger (steps, still/walk/run, rough distance) and cannot be a pet finder: no GPS chip, BLE is room range, historical store is about 14 days. The record it wants is historical packet type 47 layout 18 (R18): unix time at byte 15, dynamic g at 41, gravity xyz at 45/49/53, cumulative step counter at 57, activity class at 63 (0 still, 1 walk, 2 run). Saturday test is a wrist walk of about 100 counted steps; pass only if byte 57 rises by about 100, class flips 0 to 1, and gravity magnitude sits near 1 g. If the counter does not move, stop and keep the app's peak detector. Then measure stride on this dog (walk and trot separately). 0.83 m in Motion.swift is a starting guess to replace. Leave the optical LEDs alone. Do not build the daily log on raw 100 Hz IMU. The notes say they are research, not a Swift build plan. The Motion.swift paragraph in 02-motion-fields.txt still describes lying at 0.05 g and sitting through 0.195 g; the app later folded those into resting.
CURIOUSWhether Jared wants the wrist 100-step test of byte 57 before any R18 decoder is written. Hermes also assumed a fixed collar sleeve; the working placement he has been using is the harness pocket.
WHY AIInference: Jared wanted the Hermes notes read and summarized against the app he already has, rather than opening five text files himself.

LEARNEDFor an iPhone app, Swift is the language and SwiftUI is the UI. Use both. Flutter fits when the same screens must also ship on Android. Rust fits as a library Swift calls, for a parser or a hot core, and does not replace the UI. UIKit stays for the few controls SwiftUI still wraps thinly. Max Werba is already on the right stack for one iPhone and a WHOOP strap.
WHY AIInference: Jared wanted a stack judgment while the native app is already working, rather than a survey he would assemble himself.

14:25DEEPGRAM-VOICE-AGENT · JWERBA.COM/DEEPGRAM — Parent agent asked for a research report (no repo edits) on how the Deepgram Voice Agent API can yield structured meeting details so a browser can build an Apple Calendar .ics. Questions: current function-calling docs, exact FunctionCallRequest/Response JSON, client-side vs server-side for browser .ics, whether structured output without a function is worse, schedule_meeting schema with relative dates, Apple Calendar .ics requirements (METHOD, TZID, UID, MIME, iOS Safari quirks), and a minimal America/New_York .ics.
OUTCOMEReturned a structured research report: client-side schedule_meeting (no endpoint, defer_until_eot) plus browser/server .ics. Exact message shapes, function JSON schema, minimal .ics, pitfalls, and source URLs. No files written in any repo.
LEARNEDCurrent V1 protocol (docs dated 2026-10): client-side functions are agent.think.functions[] with no endpoint. Server sends FunctionCallRequest {type, functions:[{id, name, arguments (JSON string), client_side, thought_signature?}]}. Client replies FunctionCallResponse {type, id, name, content (string)}. OpenAPI requires type/name/content; id is recommended. arguments is a string, not an object. Early-access shape used function_name/function_call_id/input object — dead. @deepgram/agents docs still say fn.input; raw WS and OpenAPI and voice-agent-python-client use arguments. Accept both. Omit endpoint so Deepgram does not HTTP the function; client_side:true means the browser must execute. defer_until_eot:true holds irreversible calls until turn confirmation; FunctionCallCancelled means stop and do not reply. No native structured-output channel; ConversationText is prose; function calling is the documented way to structure speech. For Apple Calendar: METHOD:PUBLISH not REQUEST (REQUEST wants ORGANIZER+ATTENDEE and RSVP). Prefer DTSTART/DTEND in UTC with Z to avoid VTIMEZONE; if TZID=America/New_York, include a matching VTIMEZONE (RFC 5545 New York rules: daylight 2nd Sunday March, standard 1st Sunday November, since 2007). CRLF line endings. iOS Safari ignores download on data: URLs, rejects blob: as unknown document, and data:text/calendar often fails validation. Reliable path is a same-origin HTTPS URL with Content-Type text/calendar and Content-Disposition attachment; webcal: is for subscriptions not one-shot invites. Voice demo already uses a server WS proxy, so serving the .ics from that origin is the clean path.
CURIOUSWhether the live jwerba.com/deepgram agent Settings currently include functions, and whether iOS Safari 18+ will open a same-origin text/calendar response in Calendar without a user long-press. Not tested on a device this turn.
WHY AIDocs disagree (SDK input vs protocol arguments). Needed live page extracts, not memory, before recommending a wire format another agent will implement.

OUTCOMEWrote the audit and three-tier roadmap to the session plan file and presented it for approval. No application code changed. Recommendation: add a labeled Live mode rather than ripping out the batch path. Tier 1 is Flux listen + Flux TTS + BYO GLM, ForceEndTurn on Send, deferred send_invite and save_opportunity, and a Nova-3 Audio Intelligence post-call. Tier 2 is the turn-event strip and coaching from word times and sentiment segments. Multi-agent, telephony, medical/pharma, and self-hosted stay talk tracks. Implementation waits until Jared says to build a tier.
LEARNED2026 Voice Agent is one socket, wss://agent.deepgram.com/v1/agent/converse, Settings not SettingsConfiguration. Flux listen is flux-general-en version v2 on /v2/listen. eot_threshold 0.5-1.0 default 0.7, 1.0 suppresses natural EOT and you drive turns with ForceEndTurn. eager_eot_threshold 0.3-0.9 must be <= eot_threshold and can raise LLM calls 50-70%. eot_timeout_ms default 5000. smart_format cannot be used with Flux. keyterms are plain strings; a :0.15 suffix is a literal, not a weight. Aura-2 Orpheus cannot move to Flux TTS v2. Documented Flux default when speak is omitted is flux-kit-en. Set version v2 and model together. expressivity -2..2 beta, Flux only, changelog 26 Aug 2026 names self-hosted model version f94b1bd5. Interrupt needs a session-wide playback_offset or text_spoken is omitted. defer_until_eot (8 Sep 2026) holds irreversible functions until the turn confirms; FunctionCallCancelled means do not respond. Flux cannot do pre-recorded or call analytics, so the post-call pass is Nova-3 POST /v1/listen summarize=v2 sentiment intents topics, and the audio summary field is results.summary.short. Browser SDK layers are @deepgram/agents, @deepgram/react, @deepgram/ui, @deepgram/agents-widget. Browser auth is POST /v1/auth/grant with ttl_seconds. Do not put the API key in the client.
CURIOUSWhether to build the Live mode before the interview or walk in with this briefing and the working batch demo.
